title: Will there be more than 160 transit calls through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Oct 12, 2026 to Oct 18, 2026? Above 160
rules: If the number of transit calls through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait as reported by the IMF PortWatch is above 160 from Oct 12, 2026 to Oct 18, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: The total is calculated by summing daily counts from Oct 12, 2026 to Oct 18, 2026. The market will resolve no earlier than Tuesday at 9 AM following the end of the period, once complete data is available.

blind.reasoning: PortWatch traffic through Bab el-Mandeb was roughly 25-35 ships a day in mid-2026, and in earlier Houthi attack periods it rarely fell much below about 23 a day, the rate needed to clear 160 in a week. But the Houthis took physical control of the strait in mid-September and started a new round of attacks on 5 October, so traffic may now be falling. The threshold also looks set close to current levels, which makes this close to a coin flip.
blind.falsifier: PortWatch daily counts for Oct 12-18 averaging well above 25 a day (YES), or a sharp fall to below about 18 a day after major new attacks or ships being hit (NO).

final.reasoning: The 0.90 market price likely reflects recent PortWatch counts well above 160 a week, which undercuts my earlier guess that the threshold was set near current traffic. With traffic last seen at about 25-35 a day and earlier attack periods staying near or above 23 a day, I move up to 0.82. The remaining risk from the 5 October attacks is real but not clearly mispriced, so I pass.
